summary.text: Dave Min is the Democratic incumbent in the 47th District, first elected to the U.S. House in 2024. He began his career as an SEC enforcement attorney, later became a UC Irvine law professor, and served in the California State Senate from 2020 to 2024. His campaign materials emphasize abortion access, gun violence prevention, climate action and protections for domestic-violence survivors.

paragraphs.text: Born in Providence, Rhode Island, and raised in Palo Alto, California, the child of Korean immigrants; his official bio describes him as a product of California public schools.
Earned a B.S. in economics from the Wharton School and a B.A. in philosophy from the University of Pennsylvania in 1999, and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 2002.

Began his career as an enforcement attorney at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, and later worked as a policy advisor to Sen. Chuck Schumer and as an economic policy director at the Center for American Progress.
Became a law professor at UC Irvine in 2012, teaching and researching business law and focusing on banking and housing policy; his official bio says he testified six times before Congress.
Ran for Congress in 2018 in the 45th District, finishing third in the top-two primary behind Rep. Mimi Walters and Katie Porter.

Served in the California State Senate from December 2020 to 2024 after narrowly defeating Republican incumbent John Moorlach in 2020; he chaired the Natural Resources and Water Committee and authored the state's 30x30 land and coastal conservation law.

In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he says he passed 28 bills into law in the State Senate, including eight protecting domestic-violence survivors; his official bio says he authored more than 30 laws.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2024, succeeding Katie Porter; he serves on the Natural Resources Committee and the Oversight and Government Reform Committee.
According to his official bio, he lives in Irvine with his wife, Jane, and their three children.
